source_text:
τῆς πορνείας βορβορῷ. ὁ τοίνυν Παῦλος τῇ τῶν πολλῶν ὑπονοίᾳ συναπεχρήσατο
φήσας τἄλλα ἁμαρτήματα ἐκτὸς τοῦ σώματος εἶναι. ἕτεροι δέ φασι ταύτην ἔχειν τὸ
ῥητὸν τὴν διάνοιαν, ὅτι ὁ πορνεύων εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει, τοῦτ' ἔστιν εἰς τὴν
τοῦ ἰδίου σώματος σύστασιν καὶ εἰς αὐτήν, ὡς ἂν εἴποι τις, τὴν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
κατασκευὴν καὶ εἰς τὰς ἀρχὰς τῆς ἡμετέρας γενέσεως, ὡσανεὶ ἔλεγεν· παύσαιο
οὕτως διὰ τῆς παρανόμου μίξεως ὑβρίζων εἰς τὸ τῆς φύσεως ἐργαστήριον ἐξ οὗ καὶ
τὸ σὸν σῶμα βεβλάστηκεν. ἕτεροι δὲ ὡς σπουδὴ τῷ Παύλῳ, φασί, συγγνώμης
κρεῖττον δεῖξαι τὸ τῆς πορνείας ἁμάρτημα. καὶ εἰπὼν ἀνωτέρω· οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι τὰ
σώματα ὑμῶν μέλη Χριστοῦ ἐστιν καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς, καὶ δείξας ἐκ τούτου ὡς ὁ πορνεύων
περὶ τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ πλημμελεῖ, οὕτως ἐπιφέρει πᾶν ἁμάρτημα καὶ ἑξῆς· ὁ μὲν
γὰρ λοίδορος ἢ ἅρπαξ ἢ πλεονέκτης εἰς ἄνθρωπον ἐπλημμέλησεν ὃν ἐλοιδόρησεν ἢ
ἠδίκησεν, ὁ δὲ πορνεύσας εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ἁμαρτάνει, ὅπερ ἐστὶ μέλη Χριστοῦ.
ἡνίκα γὰρ διὰ τῆς υἱοθεσίας τοῦ πνεύματος εἰς σῶμα τελεῖ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὐ πορνείαν
μόνον ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀσέβειαν ἂν ἐγκληθήσεται ὡς τὰ μέλη τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποιῶν πόρνης
μέλη, καὶ εἰς τὸ ἴδιον σῶμα ὡς εἰς ναὸν ὑβρίζων Χριστοῦ. διὸ καὶ ἐπάγει· ἢ οὐκ
οἴδατε ὅτι τὸ σῶμα ὑμῶν ναὸς τοῦ ἐν ὑμῖν ἁγίου πνεύματός ἐστιν, οὗ ἔχετε ἀπὸ θεοῦ
καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς; τὸ γὰρ τῆς πορνείας ἁμάρτημα περὶ τὸ σῶμα ὡς περὶ θεοῦ ναὸν
ἁμαρτάνετε, καὶ φυγαδεύει τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐχ ὅτι τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων
ἀνεύθυνα–πάντα γὰρ ἔκπτωσιν ἔχει τῆς βασιλείας–ἀλλ' ὅτι πρὸς τὸ προκείμενον
ἐσπούδασε χαλεπωτέραν ἀποφῆναι τὴν πορνείαν ἁπάντων, πρόρριζον τὸ πάθος
ἀνασπᾶσαι βουλόμενος ὡς ἀσεβέστερον παρὰ Korινθίων ἁμαρτανόμενον· ὅλως γάρ,
φησίν, ἐν ὑμῖν ἀκούεται πορνεία καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. 1 Kor 6,Ὁ πορνεύσας καὶ ἀσεβείας
ἐστιν ὑπεύθυνος· τὸ γὰρ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα ἐνυβρίσας τὸν ναὸν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος
ἐμόλυνεν. ταῦτα δὲ λέγει, ἐπειδή τινες καταφρονήτως ἐπόρνευον, μικρόν τι πταῖσμα
ἢ οὐδὲ 249,ξολ2 πταῖσμα ἡγούμενοι τὴν πορνείαν, μηδὲ Μωϋσέως ἐν τῇ δεκαλόγῳ
αὐτοῦ μνημονεύσαντος. τιμὴ δὲ τὸ σωτήριον αἷμα τοῦ Χριστοῦ ὃ δέδωκεν λύτρον
ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν. δοξάσατε οὖν τὸν θεὸν μὴ μόνον ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ
σώματι, ἵνα καὶ φύσις καὶ προαίρεσις καὶ χάρισμα δοξάσῃ τὸν θεόν. ∆οξάσατε δὴ τὸν
θεὸν ἐν τῷ σώματι ὑμῶν καὶ ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ὑμῶν. μὴ μόνον ἐν τῷ χαρίσματι ἀλλὰ
καὶ ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἵνα καὶ φύσις καὶ προαίρεσις καὶ χάρις διὰ συμφωνίας δοξάσῃ τὸν
εὐεργέτην. ἄλλοι δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὴν ψυχὴν ἐξειλήφασιν. 1 Kor 7,1 Ταῦτα τῷ κλήρῳ
ἀντέγραψεν· παρ' αὐτοῦ γὰρ καὶ ἐγράφετο τῷ ἀποστόλῳ. τὴν μὲν οὖν πορνείαν
ἐκώλυσεν ὡς παράνομον, τὴν δὲ κοινωνίαν τοῦ γάμου ὡς εὐσεβῆ καὶ πορνείας
ἀπαλλακτικὴν συνεχώρησεν, τὴν δὲ ἐγκράτειαν ὡς τελειοτέραν ἐπῄνεσεν. 1 Kor 7,2–
4 ∆ιδάσκει ὅτι οἱ συνεζευγμένοι γάμῳ μᾶλλον ἀλλήλων ἢ ἑαυτῶν δεσπόζουσιν.
καλὸν ὀφείλημα τοῖς συνοικοῦσιν, ὅταν πρὸς τῇ ἄλλῃ συμφωνίᾳ ταύτην ὡς χρέως
ἀλλήλοις ἀποδιδόναι γινώσκουσιν. οἰκονομικῶς δὲ τοσαύτῃ συγκαταβάσει ἐχρήσατο
ὁ ἀπόστολος, ἵνα τὴν πορνείαν ἐκκόψῃ, τὴν κακίστην νόσον, διδάξας ὅτι οἱ
συνεζευγμένοι γάμῳ μᾶλλον ἀλλήλων ἢ ἑαυτῶν δεσπόζουσιν. 1 Kor 7,5Ἐπειδὴ
ἀλλήλων εἶπεν εἶναι δούλους, ἀκολούθως λέγει ὅτι οὐ χρὴ ἀλλήλους ἀποστερεῖν
ἑαυτῶν, εἰ μὴ ἄρα κατὰ συμφωνίαν εὐσεβῆ, ἵνα μήτε πορνείας ἀλλήλων αἴτιοι
γένωνται, μηδὲ τὴν ἐπ' ἀλλήλοις δεσποτείαν διαφθείρωσιν παρὰ γνώμην ἀλλήλων
διϊστάμενοι. 1 Kor 7,6–7 Συγγινώσκων τῇ φύσει τοῦ σώματος λέγω ὡς χρὴ ὑμᾶς
πάλιν συνελθεῖν, ἐπεὶ οὐ πάντως τοῦτο λέγω ἀποκλείων ὑμῶν τὴν ἐγκράτειαν·
θέλω γὰρ πάντας ἐν ἐγκρατείᾳ εἶναι ὡς καὶ ἐμαυτόν. 1 Kor 7,8–9 Ταῖς χήραις καὶ τοῖς
ἀγάμοις ἀνδράσι τοῖς μὴ παρθενίαν ἀσκήσασιν συμβουλεύει ἐγκρατεύεσθαι· εἰ δὲ
ἡττῶντο τῆς σαρκός, γαμεῖν δείξας, ὅτι μέγα ἡ ἐγκράτεια. ὅμως συγχωρεῖ τὸν γάμον
ὡς δεσμὸν καλόν. 250 1 Kor 7,10–11 Τὸ γυναῖκα ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς μὴ χωρισθῆναι οὐκ ἂν
εἶπεν περὶ τῶν διὰ τὸ ἀποτάσσεσθαι καὶ ἀνακεῖσθαι τῷ Χριστῷ χωριζομένων.Ἢ τῷ
ἀνδρὶ καταλλαγήτω ἢ μενέτω ἄγαμος περὶ τῶν διά τινα μάχην διϊσταμένων
δείκνυται.Ἄνω περὶ χωρισμοῦ εἶπεν τοῦ διὰ ἐγκράτειαν, ὧδε περὶ τοῦ διὰ ἐρεσχελίας
γινομένου. εἶτα εἶπεν· οὐκ ἐγὼ ἀλλ' ὁ κύριος· ἔστι γάρ τι ὃ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λέγει ὁ
ἀπόστολος, οὐχὶ πάντα δὲ ὁ κύριος δι' ἑαυτοῦ. φησὶ δὲ ὅτι παραγγέλλω ὑμῖν ἤδη ἃ ὁ
κύριος παρήγγειλεν ἐν τοῖς Εὐαγγελίοις περὶ τῶν γεγαμηκότων εἰπὼν ἃ ὁ θεὸς
pass_a_gloss: (Continuing: dips his whole self in the) mire of fornication. So Paul made use together with (them) of the opinion of the many, having said the other sins are outside the body. Others say the saying has this meaning: that the one fornicating sins against his own body, that is, against the constitution of his own body and against, as one might say, the very structure of man and against the beginnings of our birth, as if he said: may you stop thus outraging, through the unlawful mixing, the workshop of nature from which your body also sprouted. Others (say) that Paul was eager, they say, to show the sin of fornication (as) greater than pardon. And having said above 'do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ' and the following, and having shown from this that the one fornicating offends regarding the members of Christ, so he adds 'every sin' and the following: for the slanderer or robber or greedy (man) offended against a man whom he slandered or wronged, but the one who fornicated sins against his own body, which is members of Christ. For when through the adoption of the Spirit he belongs to the body of Christ, he will be charged not only with fornication but also with impiety, as making the members of Christ members of a prostitute, and outraging his own body as a temple of Christ. Therefore he adds: 'or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit in you, whom you have from God' and the following? For the sin of fornication you sin regarding the body as regarding a temple of God, and it puts to flight the Holy Spirit; not that the rest of the sins (are) unaccountable - for all have falling-out from the kingdom - but that toward the matter at hand he was eager to declare fornication harsher than all, wishing to pull out the passion by the roots as being sinned more impiously by the Corinthians: for 'actually', he says, 'fornication is heard among you' and the following (1 Cor 5:1). [Label '1 Kor 6,' (verse missing; lemmas are 6:19-20).] The one who fornicated is liable also to impiety: for having outraged his own body he defiled the temple of the Holy Spirit. And he says these things since some fornicated contemptuously, considering fornication a small slip or not even [page 249, col. 2 marker] a slip, Moses not having mentioned (it) in his decalogue. And price (is) the saving blood of Christ which he gave as ransom for us. So glorify God not only in the gift but also in the body, so that both nature and choice and gift may glorify God. (Unmarked second form:) 'So glorify God in your body and in your spirit.' Not only in the gift but also in the body, so that both nature and choice and grace may through harmony glorify the benefactor. Others have taken the spirit (to be) the soul. [Label 1 Cor 7:1.] He wrote these back to the clergy: for by it also (things) were written to the apostle. So he forbade fornication as unlawful, allowed the partnership of marriage as pious and removing fornication, and praised self-control as more perfect. [Label 1 Cor 7:2-4.] He teaches that those yoked in marriage are masters of each other rather than of themselves. A fine debt for those living together, when besides the other harmony they know to render this to each other as a debt. By way of management the apostle used so great a condescension, in order to cut out fornication, the worst disease, having taught that those yoked in marriage are masters of each other rather than of themselves. [Label 1 Cor 7:5.] Since he said they are slaves of each other, consistently he says that they must not deprive each other of themselves, unless by pious agreement, so that they neither become causes of each other's fornication, nor destroy the mastery over each other by separating against each other's mind. [Label 1 Cor 7:6-7.] Making allowance for the nature of the body I say that you must come together again, since I do not at all say this shutting out your self-control; for I want all to be in self-control as also myself. [Label 1 Cor 7:8-9.] To the widows and the unmarried men who did not practise virginity he advises to be self-controlled; but if they were defeated by the flesh, to marry, having shown that self-control (is) great. Nevertheless he allows marriage as a good bond. [page 250; Label 1 Cor 7:10-11.] 'The wife not to be separated from the husband' he would not have said about those separated because of renouncing and dedicating themselves to Christ. 'Or let her be reconciled to the husband or remain unmarried' is shown (to be) about those standing apart because of some fight. Above he spoke about the separation because of self-control, here about the one happening because of bickering. Then he said 'not I but the Lord': for there is something which the apostle says from himself, and the Lord (did) not (say) all things through himself. And he says: I charge you already what the Lord charged in the Gospels about those married, saying 'what God (… continues in the next section).
pass_b_english: …mire of fornication. So Paul fell in with the common opinion when he said that the other sins are outside the body. Others say the text means this: the fornicator sins against his own body, that is, against the very make-up of his own body, against the very structure of a human being, so to speak, and against the origins of our birth. It is as if he said: stop outraging, by unlawful intercourse, the workshop of nature from which your own body also sprang. Others again say that Paul was eager to show that the sin of fornication is beyond pardon. He had said above, "Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ?" and so on, and had shown from this that the fornicator offends against the members of Christ. So he goes on, "Every sin," and the rest. The slanderer, the robber or the grasping man has offended against the person he slandered or wronged, but the fornicator sins against his own body, which is the members of Christ. Once a man has become part of the body of Christ through the adoption the Spirit gives, he will be charged not with fornication only but with impiety as well, since he makes the members of Christ the members of a prostitute and outrages his own body as Christ's temple. That is why he adds, "Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God," and so on. In the sin of fornication you sin against the body as against God's temple, and it drives the Holy Spirit away. Not that the other sins go unpunished, for every one of them costs a man the kingdom; but, given the case in hand, he was eager to declare fornication the worst of all. He wanted to tear the passion out by the roots, since the Corinthians were committing it with particular impiety: "It is actually reported," he says, "that there is fornication among you" (1 Corinthians 5:1), and so on.

On 1 Corinthians 6:19–20: The fornicator is guilty of impiety as well, for by outraging his own body he has defiled the temple of the Holy Spirit. He says this because some were committing fornication with contempt, thinking it a small slip, or no slip at all, since Moses did not even mention it in his Ten Commandments. The price is the saving blood of Christ, which he gave as a ransom for us. Glorify God, then, not only in the gift but in the body as well, so that nature, will and gift may all glorify God.
The second catena form adds: "Glorify God, then, in your body and in your spirit." Others have taken "spirit" to mean the soul.

On 1 Corinthians 7:1: He wrote this in reply to the clergy, for it was they who had written to the apostle. He forbade fornication as unlawful, allowed the partnership of marriage as godly and as a release from fornication, and praised continence as the more perfect way.

On 1 Corinthians 7:2–4: He teaches that those joined in marriage have authority over each other rather than over themselves. It is a fine debt for those who live together when, besides the rest of their harmony, they know to pay each other this one as something owed. The apostle stooped so far as a matter of wise management, to cut out fornication, the worst of diseases, by teaching this.

On 1 Corinthians 7:5: Since he had said that they are each other's servants, he goes on, consistently, to say that they must not deprive each other of themselves, except by a godly agreement. Otherwise they may become the cause of each other's fornication, or ruin their authority over each other by parting against each other's will.

On 1 Corinthians 7:6–7: It is in allowance for the nature of the body that I say you should come together again, since I am not saying this to shut out continence for you; I want everyone to be continent, as I am myself.

On 1 Corinthians 7:8–9: He advises widows, and unmarried men who have not taken up virginity, to be continent; but if the flesh got the better of them, to marry. He shows by this that continence is a great thing; yet he allows marriage as a good bond.

On 1 Corinthians 7:10–11: He would not have said that a wife must not separate from her husband about those who separate in order to renounce the world and give themselves to Christ. "Let her be reconciled to her husband, or remain unmarried" is plainly about those who part because of some quarrel. Above he spoke of separation for the sake of continence; here, of separation that comes from bickering. Then he said, "not I but the Lord," because there are things the apostle says on his own, and the Lord did not say everything in person. He means: I charge you with what the Lord already charged in the Gospels about married people, when he said, "What God…

lemmas.gloss: go along with, make use of together

choices.term: Δοξάσατε δὴ τὸν θεὸν ... τὸν εὐεργέτην. ἄλλοι δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα τὴν ψυχὴν ἐξειλήφασιν.
choices.english: collapsed; lemma and last sentence printed after 'The second catena form adds:'
choices.why: Unmarked second form of the 6:20 note: 'not only in the gift but in the body ... nature, will and grace' repeats the first form. The lemma quotation and 'Others have taken spirit to mean the soul' have no counterpart.
The edition's label lacks a verse number; the lemmas quoted (the price, glorify God in your body) are 6:19-20.
The note repeats 'those joined in marriage have authority over each other rather than over themselves' at its end; the English refers back instead of printing it twice. Nothing is dropped.
κλῆρος in this period is the clergy.
In the marriage chapter the word means sexual abstinence; 'continence' keeps that sense.
